2.text: the Chukchee and the Yakut. The Yakut, no less than the Russians, would

3.text: consider such a marriage as humiliating; but the Yakut are much stronger

4.text: than the Russians psychically and economically, nor do they suffer so much

5.text: from hunger as the Russian creoles or the Tungus. Moreover, they have

6.text: horses of their own, horned cattle, and even reindeer, and Chukchee reindeer

7.text: are not so attractive to them.

8.text: The Marriage-Rite. — The most important part of the marriage-rite of

9.text: the Reindeer Chukchee is the anointment of the bride and groom with the

10.text: blood of the sacrificial animal. This occurs either at the house of the groom,

11.text: or, if the latter is to become an adopted son-in-law, at the house of the

12.text: bride. The ceremony is relatively simple: the groom goes to his father-in-law

13.text: to fetch his bride, and brings her to his settlement. The bride, who drives

14.text: her own reindeer, is at times accompanied by her nearest relatives.

15.text: The party arrives at the settlement of the groom, where the reindeer

16.text: are unharnessed. The small pole-sledge on which the poles of the tent are

17.text: carried is put behind the tent, on the spot where sacrifices are usually made;

18.text: while the travelling-sledges of the bride and groom stand on both sides at

19.text: some distance. Then the sacrificial reindeer is killed for the anointment.

20.text: Other sacrifices, bloody and bloodless, are made to the dawn and the zenith.

21.text: Fire-drills and charm-strings are placed on the sledges. Then the couple is

22.text: anointed with the blood of the reindeer, one or two members of the groom’s

23.text: family generally also undergoing the ceremony, in order that the bride may

24.text: not feel lonesome. Then the groom and the bride paint on their faces the

25.text: family mark of the groom. Thus the woman renounces the sacrificial anoint-

26.text: ment of her family, as well as her hearth and kin, and binds herself to another

27.text: hearth and another kin. Further, the woman anoints the sledges with blood,

28.text: and “feeds” the holy objects of the household with reindeer-marrow. She
